description: Displayed in Hangar 1 at Hendon in the markings of a day bomber coded C. One of very few surviving DH.9A airframes. Confirmed present October 2025.
aliases: DH9A; Airco DH.9A; de Havilland DH.9A

description: Ex-Red Arrows display aircraft coded 3, hung in Hangar 1. Maintenance serial 8640M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Full-scale non-flying mock-up (JSF-1) displayed in Hangar 1; it is a representation, not a real airframe. Carries UK mock-up identity BAPC.341.
aliases: F35; Joint Strike Fighter; BAPC 341; JSF-1; JSF1

description: Flying boat displayed in Hangar 1 in the markings NS-Z of No. 201 Squadron; visitors can walk through the hull. Confirmed present October 2025.
Battle of Britain-era airframe displayed in Hangar 1 in the markings ZD-F of No. 222 Squadron. Confirmed present October 2025.
Search and rescue Sea King coded A displayed in Hangar 1. Confirmed present October 2025.
Flying replica built in New Zealand and displayed in the First World War in the Air hall wearing the false German identity D.7343/17; it is a reproduction, not an original Albatros.
Original Avro 504K trainer, later civil G-EBJE and instructional airframe 9205M, displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
Original pre-1914 Bleriot racing monoplane taken over by the Royal Flying Corps; suspended in the First World War in the Air hall.
Original Bristol Fighter displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
Original Caudron G.3 in French markings, displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
Original German Air Service Fokker D.VII surrendered under the Armistice; displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.

Early B.E.2b airframe displayed in the First World War in the Air hall; substantially reconstructed and described by some sources as a reproduction. The museum's own collection entry carries no serial.
Full-size reproduction F.E.2b built for the museum and completed in 2009 for the First World War in the Air hall; it is a new-build, not an original airframe.

Two-seat corps reconnaissance aircraft in the First World War in the Air hall, marked A3930 coded B of No. 9 Squadron; the museum lists the marking rather than a confirmed original serial and some sources call it a reproduction.
Original S.E.5a, later civil G-EBIC, displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
Original Sopwith F.1 Camel coded B, displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
The only Sopwith Dolphin on display anywhere; a composite restoration completed by the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre incorporating parts of D5329.
The only surviving original Sopwith Triplane, displayed in the First World War in the Air hall.
Full-size reproduction Gunbus built in 1966 for the film Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines and later acquired by the museum; it is a replica, not an original.
Cierva C.30A autogiro built under licence by Avro, displayed in the Historic Hangars. Confirmed present October 2025.
Displayed in the Historic Hangars in the markings BA of No. 11 Squadron; maintenance serial 8961M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Displayed coded 86 in No. 1 Flying Training School markings; maintenance serial 9166M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Ex-Portuguese Air Force Beaufighter returned to the UK in 1965; maintenance serial 7931M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Composite Beaufort restoration coded L displayed in the Historic Hangars; assembled from Australian-built components.
The only surviving Bristol Bulldog, formerly civil G-ABBB; displayed in the Historic Hangars.

Sycamore displayed in the Historic Hangars. The museum's own web entry names its Sycamore as HR.14 XJ918, but survivor records place XJ918 on loan to the Ulster Aviation Society and identify the Hendon airframe as HR.12 WV783 (ex G-ALSP); serial needs confirming on site.

Elementary trainer displayed in the Historic Hangars; used on RAF Exercise Northern Venture. A Chipmunk also appears on the RAF Museum's 2025 Midlands disposal list, so which airframe is where needs checking on site.
Early single-seat Vampire coded N in No. 601 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 7200M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Winner of the 1953 London to Christchurch air race; maintenance serial 8369M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Regia Aeronautica biplane fighter force-landed in Suffolk in November 1940 and given the RAF serial BT474; wears Italian marking MM5701 and code 13-95.
Forward fuselage and salvaged remains only, recovered from Norway; displayed as a wreck in the Historic Hangars.
Displayed in No. 609 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 7930M. Confirmed present October 2025.

Fuselage recovered from Russia and rebuilt by the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre at Cosford, transferred to Hendon and displayed coded PL-K; maintenance serial 8386M. Confirmed at Hendon October 2025.
Hawker's own demonstrator, civil registered G-ABMR and displayed in the false military markings J9941; the museum's long-standing flying and display airframe.
Displayed coded 8 in No. 43 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 8863M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Battle of Britain veteran displayed in the markings AF-F of No. 607 Squadron; maintenance serial 8373M.
Displayed in post-war target-towing markings as a Tempest TT.5.
The only complete surviving Hawker Typhoon; returned from the Smithsonian in 1968 and displayed in the Historic Hangars.
Royal Australian Air Force Hudson coded SF-R; the RAF contract serial for this airframe was FH174. Confirmed present October 2025.
Flew the 1979 Atlantic crossing anniversary flight; displayed in No. 56 Squadron markings coded I; maintenance serial 9152M.

Werknummer 4101, captured in Kent in November 1940 and given the RAF serial DG200; displayed unpainted with Luftwaffe code 12. This is the Hendon Bf 109 - the museum's Bf 109G-2 is at the Midlands site.
Advanced trainer displayed in the Historic Hangars; later Dutch and civil use before preservation.
aliases: Harvard IIB; T-6; T6; AT-6; AT6

description: Communications aircraft, maintenance serial 8938M; ex-No. 60 Squadron at RAF Wildenrath. The museum's own web entry still shows it at the Midlands site but survivor records place it inside at Hendon as of October 2025.
Maintenance serial 8388M. Moved from the Midlands site to Hendon; confirmed inside at Hendon October 2025 although the museum's web entry still lists it at Midlands.
Hoverfly I, the RAF's first helicopter; also quoted as KK995 in some records. Displayed in the Historic Hangars.
Composite reconstruction marked E6655 coded B of No. 1 Squadron. The museum's collection entry records it as not currently on display.
Restored wooden hull of a Southampton flying boat, recovered after use as a houseboat; hull only, no wings.
Battle of Britain veteran displayed in the markings PR-F of No. 609 Squadron; maintenance serial 8384M.
Displayed wearing the false identity TB675 coded 4D-V of No. 74 Squadron; maintenance serial 7293M.
Last-generation Griffon Spitfire, maintenance serial 7288M. The museum's collection entry records it as not currently on display; it has been reported as stored and likely to return to public view.
Royal Canadian Air Force flying boat coded QN, later civil in British Columbia; the only complete Stranraer.
Air observation post aircraft, later civil G-AIXA; displayed in the Historic Hangars.
aliases: Auster I; Taylorcraft Plus D; G-AIXA

description: Tandem-rotor transport helicopter coded O; maintenance serial 8367M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Queen's Flight VIP Wessex in royal transport markings. Confirmed present October 2025.
Air Training Corps primary glider. The museum's collection entry records it as not currently on display.
Fuselage only. Recorded in survivor listings as held at Hendon; not shown on the museum's public collection pages, so treat as reserve collection rather than gallery display.
Twin-engine advanced trainer coded G, displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Fuselage displayed in the Bomber Hall coded 68 and marked as W2068; survivor records identify the airframe itself as LT773. The museum's own entry gives the serial as W2068.
S-Sugar, the Bomber Hall centrepiece, in the markings PO-S of No. 467 Squadron RAAF with more than 100 operations recorded on its nose; maintenance serial 7325M.
V-bomber displayed in No. 617 Squadron markings; the Bomber Hall was built around it in 1982. Maintenance serial 8733M.
Flying Fortress in United States Army Air Forces markings, displayed in the Bomber Hall. The museum's own collection page for this airframe carries no serial.
Liberator VI coded F and named Snake, recovered from India; displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Curtiss P-40N in RAF Kittyhawk IV markings, displayed in the Bomber Hall.

The Chipmunk in which the Duke of Edinburgh learned to fly; later with Aberdeen University Air Squadron. Confirmed at Hendon October 2025 although the museum's web entry lists it at the Midlands site.
The only substantially complete Fairey Battle, recovered from Iceland; displayed coded VO-S of No. 98 Squadron.
Recovered from Lake Hoklingen in Norway in 1973 and conserved unrestored as found; coded TL-S of No. 35 Squadron; maintenance serial 8465M.
Nose section only, named Lucky Lou, displayed in the Bomber Hall. Maintenance serial 8910M.
Luftwaffe bomber coded NT+SL, displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Volksjaeger jet, Werknummer 120227, coded red 2; given the RAF serial VN679 after capture. Maintenance serial 7607M.
Anti-tank Stuka coded RI+JK, one of only two surviving Ju 87s; displayed in the Bomber Hall.
The only surviving Kawasaki Ki-100, in Imperial Japanese Army markings coded 24; brought to Britain for evaluation in 1945. The museum's entry gives no serial.
Night fighter with SN-2 radar aerials, one of very few surviving Bf 110s; displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Komet rocket-powered interceptor displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Dinah high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft in Imperial Japanese Army markings; the only surviving example. The museum's entry gives no serial.

Mustang displayed in the Bomber Hall in the United States Army Air Forces markings 413317 coded VF-B and named Donald Duck; the museum quotes the display marking rather than a confirmed construction identity.
Thunderbolt II in RAF markings, displayed in the Bomber Hall.

Recovered sections of the only substantial Stirling remains in the collection, coded QQ-E. Some published lists place Stirling sections at the Midlands site; survivor records placed LK488 at Hendon in March 2025.
Slingsby T.31B Air Training Corps glider, c/n 844.
Army co-operation aircraft coded JR-M; maintenance serial 8377M. Displayed in the Bomber Hall.
Japanese piloted rocket-powered suicide attack aircraft displayed in the Bomber Hall; the museum's entry gives no serial.
Displayed in Hangar 6 in the special markings applied for the Harrier's 2010 retirement. The museum's own collection page for this airframe carries no serial. Confirmed present October 2025.
aliases: Harrier GR9; Harrier GR9A; Harrier II

description: Forward fuselage section only, presented in RAF markings in Hangar 6.
DA2, the second Eurofighter development aircraft, displayed in Hangar 6 in its black high-visibility test scheme. The museum's own collection page carries no serial.
United States Air Force Predator remotely piloted aircraft displayed in Hangar 6.
Gulf War veteran coded R with mission markings; maintenance serial 9169M. Confirmed present October 2025.
Cockpit section only of a United States Air Force weather reconnaissance Hercules, displayed in Hangar 6.
Gulf War veteran named Bob, coded AJ-J in No. 617 Squadron markings. Confirmed present October 2025.
Coded AD; maintenance serial 9019M. Confirmed present October 2025.
